summary.business: Avanti Feeds Limited is primarily engaged in the manufacturing and sale of shrimp feed, which is the core of its operations. The company also operates through subsidiaries in shrimp processing and export (Avanti Frozen Foods) and the pet food business (Avanti Pet Care), which imports and sells pet food under the 'Avant Furst' brand and is in the process of setting up a domestic manufacturing plant. The company serves the aquaculture sector, primarily shrimp farmers, and international seafood markets.

endMarkets: Indian aquaculture (shrimp farming)|International seafood markets (via subsidiary exports)

risks.note: The company's operations are heavily concentrated in shrimp feed, with sales of 5,62,060 MTs in FY26. Any adverse shift in shrimp aquaculture demand, disease outbreaks, or regulatory changes could materially impact revenue.

The company has significant foreign exchange outflows (Rs. 19,882.45 Lakhs) against limited inflows (Rs. 1,520.91 Lakhs), exposing it to currency volatility that could affect input costs and profitability.

Sealuxe B.V., Netherlands, generated no turnover and incurred a loss, while associate Patikari Power Private Limited reported a net loss of Rs. 415.95 Lakhs, indicating potential capital erosion and drag on consolidated returns.

As a listed entity, the company must continuously comply with SEBI Listing Regulations, Companies Act, and other statutory requirements. Any non-compliance could lead to penalties or reputational damage.

Operations are energy-intensive; reliance on conventional power and open-access procurement exposes the company to price volatility and supply disruptions, despite ongoing investments in solar and efficiency measures.

one-line thesis: Consolidated FY26 was a strong year (gross income INR 6,279 cr +8.9%; PBT INR 882 cr +20%) driven mainly by the Frozen/Export division (FY PBT more than doubled to INR 178 cr on +20% volume, better realizations and weak rupee), but the near-term story is about to invert: fish-meal price **doubled (INR 100→240/kg) in two months** and soya-meal jumped ~45% on a Gulf War + El Niño shock, so feed margins are set to compress in Q1/H1 FY27 until price hikes pass through. The big optionality is the **~USD 15-20m IEEPA reciprocal-tariff refund** the company expects from US Customs (entries suspended pending AD/CVD reviews, refunds 12-18 months out) plus improving US/EU shrimp demand — but management is openly unable to even budget FY27 given the uncertainty.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Feed volume:** FY27 feed sales ~5,80,000 MT (vs 5,62,060 MT FY26, ~+3%). Industry shrimp production CY26 est. 8-9 lakh MT → total feed consumption 11-12 lakh MT.
- **Export volume:** FY27 frozen-shrimp exports ~19,000 MT (vs 16,976 MT FY26, ~+12%); management defended this as deliberately step-by-step (quality/food-safety constrained), not aggressive despite EU-FTA access.
- **Feed price hikes:** another feed price increase coming "in the next few days / one week-10 days" to absorb the RM spike; quantum being finalized against market acceptability.
- **Pet food:** scaling 53 → 100 MT now, target ~800 MT by year-end; 31 distributors / 13 cities; new SKUs (treats, economy food, wet food) coming.
- **Capex:** "no big capex in the next two years" for feed or processing (growth via utilization, not capacity). Pet-food Hyderabad plant land converted, designs being finalized — construction only after DPR + govt approvals.
- **Overall:** group revenue + profit growth targeted ~10-15% over 2-3 yrs ("a big achievement" given uncertainty); management explicitly says it cannot yet prepare an FY27 budget.
order book & pipeline:
- Not an order-book business. Visibility = farmer stocking cycle: Q1 (Apr-May-Jun) is peak shrimp-culture season and is "progressing without much hurdles"; Q2 (Jul-Sep) equally important to complete season 1. Farm-gate shrimp prices stable, export market described as "promising / looking bright" (US + EU).
- Pipeline-equivalent catalysts: EU FTA (better market access, build slowly); possible US bilateral trade deal; IEEPA tariff-refund processing.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Shrimp Feed (Avanti Feeds standalone):** FY26 gross income INR 4,538 cr (-0.2% YoY, lower Apr-25 prices), PBT INR 715 cr (+8.66%); FY volume 5,62,060 MT (vs 5,55,248). Major RMs: fish meal, soya-bean meal, wheat flour (+ fish oil, soya lecithin, soya oil). Avg consumption cost Q4: fish meal INR 130/kg (Q3 117, Q4FY25 91); soya meal INR 55 (Q3 44, Q4FY25 41); wheat flour INR 31 (down). **Current purchase prices: fish meal INR 230/kg, soya meal INR 72/kg, wheat flour INR 30/kg** — i.e. spot fish meal already INR 100 above Q4 avg.
- **Processing & Export (Avanti Frozen Foods):** FY26 gross income INR 1,741 cr (+43% YoY), PBT INR 178 cr (+107%); volume 16,976 MT (+2,827, +20%). Avanti is **importer-of-record in the US** (does its own customs clearance + delivery). Stated effective/installed capacity ~26,000-28,000 MT but seasonally constrained on raw-material availability. Heavy value-add mix (ready-to-eat/cooked, breading, shrimp drinks, Japanese preparations) — among India's larger value-added producers; food-ingredients partnership; R&D being accelerated.
- **Pet Food (Avanti Pet Care, "Avant Furst"):** cat + dog food, currently imported from Thailand to Avanti formulations (own plant pending). Q4 sales INR 151 lakh. On Amazon + Supertails; digital marketing (Instagram/Facebook). Tier-1 led, entering Tier-2/3.
- **Ecuador:** Avanti has invested into Ecuador shrimp in partnership with a union/co-op — a global-supply-chain hedge alongside India.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **IEEPA tariff refund (key optionality):** US Supreme Court 20-Feb-2026 (6-3) ruled IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs; reciprocal tariffs invalidated; CBP stopped collecting IEEPA tariffs from 24-Feb-2026. Avanti Frozen (importer-of-record) will file ACE-portal entries; estimated refund ~USD 15-20m; US bank account already opened (a refund pre-condition). Caveat: Indian frozen-shrimp entries since 1-Apr-2025 are suspended pending AD/CVD administrative reviews → refunds expected only as suspension lifts, ~12-18 months.
- **EU FTA:** improved access; multi-year volume build (quality/safety gated).
- **Value-added shrimp:** structurally higher margin than peers; deliberate balance vs commodity throughput (more value-add = lower physical output).
- **Pet food:** early but management is bullish ("expecting a lot of growth").
- **Geographic diversification:** China +24%, EU +36%, Japan +5% in FY26 (vs US -17.9% by volume) — reducing single-geography dependence.
margins & cost dynamics:
- **Feed margin squeeze is the headline risk:** fish meal doubled INR 100→240/kg in two months (May-Jun), soya meal +~45%, driven by Gulf War (supply) + El Niño (crop failure fear). Soya tightness from 13-lakh-ton prior-year crop shortfall; GoI raised soya MSP ~INR 380/quintal (to INR 5,708). Mitigation = feed price hikes (one taken Feb-26, only ~1 month partial impact in Q4; another imminent) — management "confident cost will be absorbed to a great extent" but not fully.
- **Export margin:** structurally above market on value-add mix; FY26 helped by FX, lower ocean freight, higher realizations. Trade-off: more value-add → lower factory output.
- **Labour-code provisions** (gratuity + leave encashment) dented both divisions' Q4 PBT.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Explicit: no big capex in feed or processing for ~2 years; growth via capacity utilization.
- Pet-food Hyderabad plant: land acquired & converted to non-agri; designs/drawings being finalized; construction post-DPR + govt approvals (own production is when "real fruits" come; until then imports from Thailand). Watch for DPR/approval timeline slippage.
capital allocation: - Conservative — no large capex committed; cash deployed into pet-food brand build (imports + marketing first, plant later) and the Ecuador investment. (Dividend policy not discussed on this call.)
risks & watch-items:
- **RM inflation (acute):** fish-meal/soya spike could compress H1 FY27 feed margins before hikes fully pass through; further escalation if El Niño hits the kharif crop.
- **Fish-meal export drain:** ~75% of India-made fish meal is exported (price + GoI incentives; 5% GST on local purchase vs nil on exports) — Avanti + FMA + CLFMA lobbying GoI to curb fish-meal exports/incentives and to allow soya-meal imports (done once before, ~2003). Policy outcome uncertain.
- **US tariff structure unresolved:** post-IEEPA, US introduced a temporary Section-122 (Trade Act 1974) global surcharge from 24-Feb-2026 for up to 150 days, initially 10% but "indications of a possible increase" — final seafood tariff still unclear.
- **Refund timing/quantum risk:** USD 15-20m still being validated; AD/CVD review suspension means 12-18-month wait.
- **Demand/biological risk:** shrimp culture depends on disease, climate, farm-gate prices; Q2 still ahead.
- **Budgeting blackout:** management cannot yet frame an FY27 budget — low forward visibility.
- **Ecuador competition** remains #1 exporter (though Ecuador "issues" emerging may help India).
management quality / tone: - Candid and operationally detailed; JMD repeatedly deferred technical questions to the right divisional ED/CFO (good bench). Honest about not being able to budget FY27 and about margin pressure; measured (not promotional) on export-growth pace, explicitly rejecting "exponential" growth in favour of step-by-step quality-gated scaling. Some answers vague on capacity ("send an email"). Realistic on pet food being a long brand-build.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The IEEPA refund (~USD 15-20m) is a real, quantified but back-ended optionality — a future other-income/PBT kicker not in current numbers, gated by AD/CVD review timing (12-18 months). Track ACE filings and the suspension-of-liquidation lift.
- Feed (the cash cow) is entering a margin air-pocket: spot fish meal (INR 230-240) is already ~INR 100 above the Q4 consumption average (INR 130), so reported feed margins likely worsen further in Q1 FY27 until the next price hike lands — a near-term negative the strong FY26 PBT masks.
- Mix is quietly de-risking from the US: US volume fell -17.9% while China/EU/Japan grew sharply; the export division (not feed) drove FY26 profit growth (+107% PBT) — Avanti is becoming less a pure feed play and more a balanced feed + value-added-export + (nascent) pet-food group.
- The fish-meal export issue is a domestic policy lever: if GoI curbs fish-meal exports/incentives, it directly relieves Avanti's single biggest input — a regulatory catalyst worth tracking.

- **Fish-meal export drain:** ~75% of India-made fish meal is exported (price + GoI incentives; 5% GST on local purchase vs nil on exports) — Avanti + FMA + CLFMA lobbying GoI to curb fish-meal exports/incentives and to allow soya-meal imports (done once before, ~2003). Policy outcome uncertain.
- **US tariff structure unresolved:** post-IEEPA, US introduced a temporary Section-122 (Trade Act 1974) global surcharge from 24-Feb-2026 for up to 150 days, initially 10% but "indications of a possible increase" — final seafood tariff still unclear.
- **Refund timing/quantum risk:** USD 15-20m still being validated; AD/CVD review suspension means 12-18-month wait.
- **Demand/biological risk:** shrimp culture depends on disease, climate, farm-gate prices; Q2 still ahead.
- **Budgeting blackout:** management cannot yet frame an FY27 budget — low forward visibility.
- **Ecuador competition** remains #1 exporter (though Ecuador "issues" emerging may help India).
management quality / tone: - Candid and operationally detailed; JMD repeatedly deferred technical questions to the right divisional ED/CFO (good bench). Honest about not being able to budget FY27 and about margin pressure; measured (not promotional) on export-growth pace, explicitly rejecting "exponential" growth in favour of step-by-step quality-gated scaling. Some answers vague on capacity ("send an email"). Realistic on pet food being a long brand-build.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The IEEPA refund (~USD 15-20m) is a real, quantified but back-ended optionality — a future other-income/PBT kicker not in current numbers, gated by AD/CVD review timing (12-18 months). Track ACE filings and the suspension-of-liquidation lift.
- Feed (the cash cow) is entering a margin air-pocket: spot fish meal (INR 230-240) is already ~INR 100 above the Q4 consumption average (INR 130), so reported feed margins likely worsen further in Q1 FY27 until the next price hike lands — a near-term negative the strong FY26 PBT masks.
- Mix is quietly de-risking from the US: US volume fell -17.9% while China/EU/Japan grew sharply; the export division (not feed) drove FY26 profit growth (+107% PBT) — Avanti is becoming less a pure feed play and more a balanced feed + value-added-export + (nascent) pet-food group.

identity.name: AVANTI FEEDS LIMITED
identity.industry: Aquaculture / Shrimp Feed & Frozen-Shrimp Processing-Exports (agri-FMCG, US-export levered)

hero.oneLiner: Consolidated FY26 was a strong year driven mainly by the Frozen/Export division, refunds 12-18 months out) plus improving US/EU shrimp demand, but management is openly unable to even budget FY27 given the uncertainty.
hero.industry: Aquaculture / Shrimp Feed & Frozen-Shrimp Processing-Exports (agri-FMCG, US-export levered)

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Avanti Feeds Limited is primarily engaged in the manufacturing and sale of shrimp feed, which is the core of its operations. The company also operates through subsidiaries in shrimp processing and export (Avanti Frozen Foods) and the pet food business (Avanti Pet Care), which imports and sells pet food under the 'Avant Furst' brand and is in the process of setting up a domestic manufacturing plant. The company serves the aquaculture sector, primarily shrimp farmers, and international seafood markets.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Avanti Frozen Foods Private Limited (AFFPL) — subsidiary: Engaged in frozen foods business.
- Avanti Pet Care Private Limited (APCPL) — subsidiary: Trading in pet food (imported from Joint Venture Partner) under Avant Furst brand; in process of acquiring land for a manufacturing plant in Hyderabad.
- Srivathsa Power Projects Private Limited (SPPPL) — subsidiary: Power generation stopped due to increased cost and non-availability of APM-gas since May 2022; no generation during the year.
- Sealuxe B.V., Netherlands — subsidiary: Capital raised during the year.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Shrimp Feed (Avanti Feeds standalone):** FY26 gross income INR 4,538 cr (-0.2% YoY, lower Apr-25 prices), PBT INR 715 cr (+8.66%); FY volume 5,62,060 MT (vs 5,55,248). Major RMs: fish meal, soya-bean meal, wheat flour (+ fish oil, soya lecithin, soya oil). Avg consumption cost Q4: fish meal INR 130/kg (Q3 117, Q4FY25 91); soya meal INR 55 (Q3 44, Q4FY25 41); wheat flour INR 31 (down). **Current purchase prices: fish meal INR 230/kg, soya meal INR 72/kg, wheat flour INR 30/kg** — i.e. spot fish meal already INR 100 above Q4 avg.
- **Processing & Export (Avanti Frozen Foods):** FY26 gross income INR 1,741 cr (+43% YoY), PBT INR 178 cr (+107%); volume 16,976 MT (+2,827, +20%). Avanti is **importer-of-record in the US** (does its own customs clearance + delivery). Stated effective/installed capacity ~26,000-28,000 MT but seasonally constrained on raw-material availability. Heavy value-add mix (ready-to-eat/cooked, breading, shrimp drinks, Japanese preparations) — among India's larger value-added producers; food-ingredients partnership; R&D being accelerated.
- **Pet Food (Avanti Pet Care, "Avant Furst"):** cat + dog food, currently imported from Thailand to Avanti formulations (own plant pending). Q4 sales INR 151 lakh. On Amazon + Supertails; digital marketing (Instagram/Facebook). Tier-1 led, entering Tier-2/3.
- **Ecuador:** Avanti has invested into Ecuador shrimp in partnership with a union/co-op — a global-supply-chain hedge alongside India.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Shrimp Feed:** Shrimp Feed
- **Pet Food:** Avant Furst

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Not an order-book business. Visibility = farmer stocking cycle: Q1 (Apr-May-Jun) is peak shrimp-culture season and is "progressing without much hurdles"; Q2 (Jul-Sep) equally important to complete season 1. Farm-gate shrimp prices stable, export market described as "promising / looking bright" (US + EU).
- Pipeline-equivalent catalysts: EU FTA (better market access, build slowly); possible US bilateral trade deal; IEEPA tariff-refund processing.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Feed volume:** FY27 feed sales ~5,80,000 MT (vs 5,62,060 MT FY26, ~+3%). Industry shrimp production CY26 est. 8-9 lakh MT → total feed consumption 11-12 lakh MT.
- **Export volume:** FY27 frozen-shrimp exports ~19,000 MT (vs 16,976 MT FY26, ~+12%); management defended this as deliberately step-by-step (quality/food-safety constrained), not aggressive despite EU-FTA access.
- **Feed price hikes:** another feed price increase coming "in the next few days / one week-10 days" to absorb the RM spike; quantum being finalized against market acceptability.
- **Pet food:** scaling 53 → 100 MT now, target ~800 MT by year-end; 31 distributors / 13 cities; new SKUs (treats, economy food, wet food) coming.
- **Capex:** "no big capex in the next two years" for feed or processing (growth via utilization, not capacity). Pet-food Hyderabad plant land converted, designs being finalized — construction only after DPR + govt approvals.
- **Overall:** group revenue + profit growth targeted ~10-15% over 2-3 yrs ("a big achievement" given uncertainty); management explicitly says it cannot yet prepare an FY27 budget.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **IEEPA tariff refund (key optionality):** US Supreme Court 20-Feb-2026 (6-3) ruled IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs; reciprocal tariffs invalidated; CBP stopped collecting IEEPA tariffs from 24-Feb-2026. Avanti Frozen (importer-of-record) will file ACE-portal entries; estimated refund ~USD 15-20m; US bank account already opened (a refund pre-condition). Caveat: Indian frozen-shrimp entries since 1-Apr-2025 are suspended pending AD/CVD administrative reviews → refunds expected only as suspension lifts, ~12-18 months.
- **EU FTA:** improved access; multi-year volume build (quality/safety gated).
- **Value-added shrimp:** structurally higher margin than peers; deliberate balance vs commodity throughput (more value-add = lower physical output).
- **Pet food:** early but management is bullish ("expecting a lot of growth").
- **Geographic diversification:** China +24%, EU +36%, Japan +5% in FY26 (vs US -17.9% by volume) — reducing single-geography dependence.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Cost pressures on key raw materials (fish meal, soya bean meal) have intensified entering FY 2026–27; the company will implement necessary price revisions as market conditions permit.
- Improving trade dynamics, the India–EU Free Trade Agreement, and the India–UK CETA are expected to support accelerated growth in processed shrimp through market diversification and value-added products.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **Feed margin squeeze is the headline risk:** fish meal doubled INR 100→240/kg in two months (May-Jun), soya meal +~45%, driven by Gulf War (supply) + El Niño (crop failure fear). Soya tightness from 13-lakh-ton prior-year crop shortfall; GoI raised soya MSP ~INR 380/quintal (to INR 5,708). Mitigation = feed price hikes (one taken Feb-26, only ~1 month partial impact in Q4; another imminent) — management "confident cost will be absorbed to a great extent" but not fully.
- **Export margin:** structurally above market on value-add mix; FY26 helped by FX, lower ocean freight, higher realizations. Trade-off: more value-add → lower factory output.
- **Labour-code provisions** (gratuity + leave encashment) dented both divisions' Q4 PBT.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: - Conservative — no large capex committed; cash deployed into pet-food brand build (imports + marketing first, plant later) and the Ecuador investment. (Dividend policy not discussed on this call.)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report does not disclose any specific capex projects, capacity expansions, or new plant commissioning plans with timelines. The business volume growth is organic, with shrimp feed sales increasing by 1.23% to 562,060 MTs in FY26. The associate Patikari Power Private Limited operates a 16 MW hydel power project in Himachal Pradesh, generating 8.75 million units of saleable energy during the year, but no expansion of this project is mentioned.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Internal contradiction - FY25 feed revenue] The segment table shows FY25 Shrimp Feed revenue of Rs 44,199.67 mn, while the Operational Highlights fiscal table shows FY25 Shrimp Feed revenues of Rs 44,289.9 mn. Both readings are quoted; the deck does not reconcile them.
- [Internal contradiction - period label] The "Quarterly & FY ended Results Snapshot" text reads "Consolidated Revenues in Q3FY26 grew 6.12% YoY at Rs 14,677 Mn", but every table in the deck places Rs 14,677.17 mn in the Q4FY26 column (Q3FY26 is Rs 13,835.2 mn). The commentary label and the tables disagree.
- [Internal contradiction - EBIT attribution] The Rs 1,980 Mn EBIT figure is written under the "Shrimp Feed" commentary heading, but the same Rs 1,980.23 mn appears in the tables as consolidated EBIT for Q4FY26; the deck does not clarify which it means.

- [Shareholding, 31 Mar 2026] Promoter 43.23%, Foreign Body 24.21%, Retail 18.11%, FPI 7.63%, DII 6.82%. Market cap ~INR 146 bn as on 09 June 2026 on 136 mn shares outstanding as on 31 Mar 2026.
